title: Newton’s First Law of Motion: Inertia
lead: A body at rest stays at rest and a body in motion keeps moving at a constant velocity unless a net external force acts on it. This section states Newton’s first law, shows that friction, and not the motion itself, is what brings a sliding object to a halt, and names the property the law describes: inertia, which is measured by mass.
objectives: Understand Newton's first law of motion.
summary_html:
• Newton’s first law of motion states that a body at rest remains at rest, or, if in motion, remains in motion at a constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force. This is also known as the law of inertia.
  • Inertia is the tendency of an object to remain at rest or remain in motion. Inertia is related to an object’s mass.
  • Mass is the quantity of matter in a substance.

exercises.prompt: Which has more mass: a kilogram of cotton balls or a kilogram of gold?

answer.solution: They are equal. A kilogram of one substance is equal in mass to a kilogram of another substance. The quantities that might differ between them are volume and density.

exercises.prompt: How are inertia and mass related?

answer.solution: Inertia is the property of a body that keeps it at rest or keeps it moving at a constant velocity, and mass is the measure of that property. A body with more mass has more inertia, which is why it is more difficult to change the motion of a large boulder than that of a basketball. Because mass is measured in kilograms by comparison with the standard kilogram, measuring the mass of a body is how the inertia it has is put into numbers, and it is also why Newton’s first law is often called the law of inertia.

exercises.prompt: What is the relationship between weight and mass? Which is an intrinsic, unchanging property of a body?

answer.solution: Mass is the quantity of matter in a body, and weight is the gravitational force that acts on that matter, so the two are closely related but they are not the same quantity and they are not measured in the same units. Mass is the intrinsic, unchanging property: the mass of an object is the same on Earth, in orbit, or on the surface of the Moon, since the number of atoms and molecules in it does not change when it is carried somewhere else. Weight does change from place to place, because it depends on the strength of the gravitational pull where the body happens to be.
